<span class="origin-badge origin-badge--onesimus">Onesimus extension</span>

Restore tree of a job chain as JSON (OVFS).

## Synopsis

```text
.ovfs_tree [jobid=<jobid>[,...]] [client=<client>] [fileset=<fileset>]
           [root=<root>] [depth=<depth>] [max_entries=<max_entries>] [json]
```

Words without brackets are required, `[ ]` marks optional parts, `a | b` alternatives, `...` a repeatable argument and `[,...]` a comma separated list.

## Description

Onesimus extension: returns the directory tree of a job chain below a directory as a restore would bring it back: per path the version from the newest job, deleted files left out, hardlinks and delta files resolved. Every node with a catalog record carries its restore identity (jobid, fileindex). No cache is needed. The chain is given by jobid= or by client= (and fileset=) for the newest state like .ovfs\_latest.

root= sets the top of the tree (default /), depth= the number of levels (default 1; directories at the limit show their entry count), max\_entries= the maximum number of nodes (default 100000; beyond it the command stops with a message). For large backups load the top with a small depth and expand directories with .ovfs\_ls. json prints one JSON line.

## Arguments {#arguments}

| Argument | Type | Values / source | Default | Flags | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jobid=` | string |  |  | list | Job ID list. |
| `client=` | resource | from [`.clients`](../dot-clients/) |  |  | Client name (latest state). |
| `fileset=` | resource | from [`.filesets`](../dot-filesets/) |  |  | FileSet name. |
| `root=` | string |  | `/` |  | Directory. |
| `depth=` | integer |  | `1` |  | Levels below root. |
| `max_entries=` | integer |  | `100000` |  | Most nodes in the result. |
| `json` | keyword |  |  |  | Print the JSON object as text. |

## Examples

Two levels below /home of a job chain:

```text
.ovfs_tree jobid=600,615,616 root=/home/ depth=2
```

The top level of the newest state as JSON:

```text
.ovfs_tree client=bareos-fd depth=1 json
```
